after.en: As ᾱ falls slowly from 1 to 0, the picture sinks little by little into the noise. The squares of the two coefficients add up to 1, so whatever the step, the total "energy" of the picture stays about the same. This formula lets training jump straight to any step without adding noise step by step.

t.en: Start from one clean image and vary timestep t to compare how much original signal and noise remain. Understand how diffusion corrupts the image before using predicted noise to recover it.
The best image generators today are called diffusion models. Their training starts the other way round: noise is added to a picture little by little until only noise is left.
How far it has gone is given by one number, ᾱ, how much of the picture is left: 1 is the original, 0 is pure noise.
Your task in this level: by the formula in the brief, work out in one step the picture after noise is added up to step t.

desc.en: Outputs √ᾱ·x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ)·ε: x₀ noised straight to step t.

brief.en: A diffusion model adds noise to a picture: x_t = √ᾱ · x₀ + √(1 − ᾱ) · ε. Output x_t by the formula.

hint.en: √ᾱ and √(1 − ᾱ) are each a single number, multiplied onto the whole picture.
